low.rationale: Heme iron is the most absorbable form and directly rebuilds iron stores.
Plant iron adds to intake; pair with vitamin C to boost absorption.
Vitamin C markedly increases absorption of non-heme iron eaten in the same meal.

high.rationale: Lowering dietary iron load can help when stores are elevated; confirm cause with a doctor.

low.rationale: Fatty fish and fortified foods are the main dietary sources of vitamin D.
Skin synthesises vitamin D from sunlight; a key non-food lever.

high.rationale: Iodine is required for thyroid hormone production; mild deficiency can raise TSH.
Selenium supports conversion of thyroid hormones.

low.rationale: B12 occurs almost only in animal foods and fortified products.

high.rationale: Adequate hydration supports calcium handling; persistent high calcium needs medical review.
Magnesium supports the stress-response system and may help temper cortisol.
Cortisol is strongly driven by sleep and stress patterns.

low.rationale: Zinc is a cofactor in testosterone production.
Adequate dietary fat supports sex-hormone synthesis.
Strength training is one of the most reliable levers for free testosterone.
Caffeine has a half-life of about five hours, so an afternoon cup is still active at bedtime.
A stable schedule is the single strongest behavioural lever on total sleep time.
Magnesium is involved in the pathways that regulate sleep, and short sleepers are often low in it.
Tryptophan is the precursor the body converts towards melatonin.

high.rationale: Fibre increases fullness per calorie, which is the mechanism behind most sustainable intake reduction.
Protein is the most satiating macronutrient and protects lean mass while weight comes down.
Liquid calories do not trigger fullness the way the same calories eaten do.

foods: progressive resistance training twice a week
high.rationale: Resistance work preserves the lean mass that determines resting energy use.

low.rationale: Adding calories in small volumes is easier to sustain than eating larger meals.
Protein supports building tissue rather than only adding fat mass.

high.rationale: Endurance training raises stroke volume, which lowers the beats needed at rest.
Being under-hydrated reduces blood volume, and the heart compensates by beating faster.

foods: limit alcohol, especially in the evening
high.rationale: Alcohol raises resting and overnight heart rate for hours after the last drink.
Potassium is central to the electrical signalling that sets heart rhythm.
